question: The rack is too tall to fit in one photo. How do I scan it?
answer:
Use MULTI mode, which joins several overlapping photos into one tall image before analysing it.

1. Tap SCAN, then the Upload tab, then MULTI (the middle of the three mode buttons: SINGLE, MULTI, VIDEO).
2. Tap Select photos and pick between 2 and 8 overlapping photos of the rack. The screen tells you "Take 2-8 overlapping photos of the rack. Any order — we'll arrange them automatically."
3. The button at the bottom counts down what is still missing — "Add 2 more photo" with nothing selected, "Add 1 more photo" with one — and once you have at least two it becomes Stitch & Analyze with the photo count in brackets. Tap it.

Once photos are in the list, the header shows "N photos · auto-arranged" and a N/8 counter. You can add more with Add more (hidden once you hit 8), reorder with the up/down arrows on each row, or remove one with the X — but you do not need to: the top-to-bottom order is worked out for you from the overlaps. The server also enforces the same limits, so fewer than 2 or more than 8 photos will not be accepted.
rootCause: MultiUploadZone caps the file list at 8 (slice(0,8)) and the CTA requires >= 2 files before it becomes Stitch & Analyze.

question: How do I see what's on the other end of a cable?
answer:
Open the rack, open Ports, then tap the Cables tab. The number on the tab is how many ports currently see a neighbour on the far end; the list itself is headed with the exact count (for example "6 LINKS").

Each row is one cable: your port number and interface on the left, the far-end device on the right, plus a tag saying whether it is a Device, an Uplink or a Switch link. Tap a row to expand it into a trace showing both ends. Where the port feeds a whole downstream network (an uplink, a switch-to-switch link, or any port with more than one device behind it), the trace lists the devices found behind it with their makers — long lists are shortened, so use "show all" to see the rest.

One thing that is not a fault: a patch panel or wall socket in the middle of a run is passive, with no electronics, so the switch cannot see it. The trace will look like the cable runs straight from the switch to the far-end device. If you keep a cable schedule, record the panel in the port label.

If the tab is empty it just means RackTrack is still reading the switch — only live ports with an LLDP neighbour or a known MAC appear here.
symptoms: what's on the end of this cable
patch panel missing from the trace
rootCause: PortsPage CablesView derives cable rows from live port data + LLDP neighbours; expanding a row mounts CableTrace.

question: How do I connect our CMDB or other data source?
answer:
This is an admin-only area (org admin or owner). Open Data Sources — from Profile it is the row under the Data Sources heading, or use Data Sources in the sidebar.

1. Tap Add connection.
2. Give it a Name (for example "My ServiceNow Dev").
3. Choose the Type. The fields below change to match it:
   - ServiceNow / CMDB — Instance ID (just the part before .service-now.com), Username, Password.
   - NetBox — Base URL, API Token (from your NetBox user profile).
   - SolarWinds Orion — Host, Username, Password.
   - CA / DX Spectrum — Base URL, Username, Password.
   - My own database (SQL) — a PostgreSQL or MySQL connection string.
   - My own database (REST) — Base URL, and an API token if it needs one.
4. Tap Save & use.

Only one connection is active at a time, and every screen reads from that one — switching it switches the source of all your data. To switch, tap Use on any other saved connection. The three-dot menu gives Edit and Delete. Connections are saved per signed-in admin account, not shared across the org.

When you Edit an existing connection the credential boxes open empty on purpose — the page says "Leave the credential fields blank to keep what's already saved." The Type is locked once a connection exists ("Type can't change after a connection is created"); to change type, create a new connection.

There is no test button, and saving is not a test: Save only checks that the required boxes are filled and then stores the credentials encrypted — it never contacts your system, so wrong credentials will save without complaint. To actually prove a ServiceNow connection works, tap Use on it (or, if it is already active, use "Refresh data from this source"). That runs a real poll and shows either "Pulled N incidents from <instance>" or "Refresh failed: …". The poll can take a few minutes on a cold developer instance.
symptoms: credentials are blank when I edit
rootCause: ConnectionsPage (/connections) behind AdminRoute; TYPE_INFO defines the per-type field schema; secrets are never preloaded into the edit form.

question: How do I approve a new organization that has signed up?
answer:
Platform owner only. Open the Organizations console (/organizations). Self-signups appear at the top under "Pending approvals" — the section only shows when at least one request is waiting — each tagged Pending with "Requested by <username> · <email>". Until you act they are locked out of everything: the server rejects every request from a pending org (403 "Your organization is awaiting approval"), not just the UI.

Three buttons on each pending row:
- Approve — sets the org active. Their waiting screen polls every 12 seconds and drops them into the app on its own (they can also hit "Check now").
- Reject — sets the org to "rejected"; they see "Request not approved" instead of the spinner. The org and all its accounts survive, so it is reversible: the org stays in "All organizations" below, and its three-dot menu offers Reactivate to let them in later.
- Remove — permanently deletes the organization (with a confirm modal). Use Reject unless you are certain.

On the All organizations cards below, the three-dot menu gives Edit (rename), Deactivate (or Reactivate), and Remove.

Important: nobody is emailed when a company signs up — the only email the system sends is the signup verification code. You find out about new requests only by opening this console, so check it.
rootCause: OrgConsolePage owner branch renders the pending list with approveOrg/rejectOrg and a removeOrg confirm modal; per-org kebab menu offers Edit / Deactivate / Remove.

question: How do I run an audit on a lab switch?
answer:
Platform owner only. Open Lab in the sidebar (it only appears for owners), or go to /lab. Anyone else sees "Restricted to platform owners."

1. The lab devices are shown as a grid of buttons, each tagged with its state: Live, Offline, No data, Disabled, or Connecting…
2. Click a device. If it is enabled and the poller is reaching it, the audit runs automatically the first time you select it — you do not need to press anything. If the device is Disabled or Offline the auto-run is deliberately skipped (the SSH attempt would just hang), and a banner explains why; press the button to force an attempt.
3. Read the result using the tab strip: Identity, Ports, VLANs, LLDP, MAC.
4. To re-run it later press Refresh audit (the button reads Run full audit if there is no result yet, and Connecting… while one is in flight). It is greyed out while polling is disabled for that device. Disable polling / Enable polling turns the background polling of that device on and off.

Two things that look wrong but are not. Results are kept per device, so flipping between devices shows you what was last seen with a note of how old it is — a stamp like "Audit as of 4m ago · live SSH pass, not polled". And the virtual Cisco switches genuinely report "—" for speed, duplex and PoE, because they have no physical link or PoE hardware.
symptoms: speed and PoE show a dash
rootCause: LabPage is owner-gated (server requireRole('owner') on /api/lab/*). Audits auto-run on first selection, are cached per device in auditsRef, and one SSH pass runs at a time. Cisco IOL has no link negotiation or PoE hardware.

question: How do I list surplus equipment for sale, and how do I search what's already listed?
answer:
Admin only (organization admin or platform owner), and the Marketplace link lives in the desktop/landscape-iPad sidebar — it is not on the phone bottom bar. Open Marketplace.

The section headings across the top are Browse, My listings, Orders, Alerts, Dashboard and Partners.

To search and filter what is listed (this toolbar only appears on the Browse tab):
- Type in the box marked "Search by title, vendor or model…". The X inside it clears your text.
- Use the category dropdown next to it — it opens on "All categories".
- Use the For sale / Wanted pair to switch between things people are selling and things people are looking for.
- When any filter is on, a "Clear filters" link appears next to the results heading (and again in the empty-results panel).

To list something:
1. Tap List an item (top right of the Marketplace header).
2. Choose For sale, or Wanted if you are looking for something rather than selling it.
3. Fill in Title (required, up to 140 characters), Vendor, Model and Category. Category is a dropdown that already has a value selected, so you only change it if the default is wrong.
4. Set Condition (New (sealed) / Refurbished / Used — working / For parts — also pre-selected) and a Price. Leave the price blank and buyers see "Make an offer". You can also set Currency (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, INR) and Quantity.
5. Add a Location and Description (up to 2000 characters) if useful. Both optional.
6. Add a photo — optional, JPG / PNG / WebP / HEIC, up to 8 MB. Wait for it to say Photo ready (it shows Uploading… first, or Upload failed if something went wrong). A wrong file type gives "Only image files are accepted (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC)."; too large gives "Image must be 8 MB or smaller."
7. Tap Publish listing (or Post request if you chose Wanted). The button reads Publishing… while it saves.

If RackTrack recognises the vendor/model as one of its partners, an "Or send buyers to a partner" box appears above the buttons — that is an alternative to publishing, not a required step.
symptoms: how do I search the marketplace
rootCause: MarketplacePage toolbar (search + category + kind segmented control) plus MarketplaceShell's default 'List an item' action into MarketplaceNewPage, which caps images at 8 MB.
